`scripts/build-blog.mjs` defines a marked `RENDERER` with no `html` method and merges it onto marked's defaults, whose `html` renderer is a passthrough, so raw `

Commits on `main` from `4b354e6` (2026-07-19) through `254484d` (2026-08-03) carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude …` trailer, and many of them also carry a `Claude-Session:` URL in the message; commits after `254484d` carry neither.

`_headers` cache rules apply only to the paths they name, so `/blog/media/**` images, `/art/essentialism/*`, every `/experiments/*/app.js` and `style.css`, `/projects/poap-saver/app.js` and the whole `/experiments/poap-vault/img/` set (over 700 WebP files) fall to the Pages default `max-age=0, must-revalidate` and are not browser-cacheable.

`/experiments/dls/` ships two unoptimized JPEGs, `HEw3HB0WoAAHoBW.jpeg` (about 706 KB) and `rzVCLxC8.jpg` (about 345 KB), that together are over 95% of the page's weight; neither `` carries `width`/`height` attributes and neither is lazy-loaded.

`art/essentialism/index.html` declares `essentialism-2022.png` with `width="1200" height="900"` while the image file itself is square (1200×1200), so the browser reserves a 4:3 box and shifts layout on decode.

`scripts/build-feed.mjs` catches a git failure, warns, and still writes a valid-looking empty feed with a hardcoded `2026-01-01` timestamp instead of throwing, so a broken build produces a signed, manifest-hashed empty feed.

`scripts/sign-release.sh` folds stderr into stdout, pipes the publish step through `tail`, and never inspects the exit status, so if every relay rejects the release event the script prints the rejections and exits 0.
`scripts/build-stamp.mjs` skips a missing page with a warning and still exits 0, and nothing compares the number of pages stamped against the expected count.

In `scripts/build-blog.mjs`, several front-matter fields (including `tags`, which is unconstrained) reach the page unescaped, and the `updated` field gets none of the `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` validation that `date` already has, landing raw in both the page and the Atom feed.

`package.json` defines a `check:readme` script that nothing runs; the build runs the rewriting variant instead, and `readme.md` is not part of the published artifact, so the drift guard on the readme can never fail anything.

The comment in `.npmrc` claims no package in the dependency tree declares an install hook, but the lockfile's `fsevents` 2.3.3 entry declares one (optional, darwin-only), so the justification written next to `ignore-scripts=true` is false.
`@chenglou/pretext` is declared in `package.json` but nothing in `scripts/` imports it, and `marked` is pinned two major versions behind the current release.

`experiments/poap-vault/publicsans.woff2` is byte-identical to `fonts/publicsans-v1.woff2` but served at a different URL, so it cannot share the cache entry and additionally inherits the default `max-age=0`.
The comment in `_redirects` says the catch-all rule covers 763 files, but the number of files it actually covers is different, so the figure in the comment is stale.

`blog/posts/art-tech-highlights.md` and `blog/posts/podcasts-public-speaking.md` each contain eleven bare `![](…)` images with no alt text, and both lack an `image_alt` front-matter field for their lead image, so about 25 content images ship with `alt=""`.

`/experiments/pendulum/` has 11 buttons, 10 range sliders and a select with no accessible names (the visible labels are unassociated sibling spans), and its CSS sets `input[type=range]:focus { outline: none; }` with no replacement focus style.

In the dark theme, `text-neutral-600` (`#525252`) on black is about 2.69:1 and is used for links in the footer build line injected by `scripts/build-stamp.mjs` on most pages, and `--ink-soft: #737373` is about 4.43:1 and is used for running heads, section labels, post meta and table headers, so dark mode fails WCAG AA for text site-wide.
`mirrors/index.html` has a `bg-zinc-900` `<pre>` block that never receives a light-theme override, so in light mode its text is about 2.29:1 against its background.
The search overlay declares `aria-modal="true"` but `search.js` has no Tab trap (it tracks `lastFocus` only), so keyboard focus escapes the dialog on the second Tab press.
Most pages carry `<meta http-equiv="content-language">`, which is an HTML5 validator error; `<html lang="en">` already covers it.
The home page's heading outline is `h1, h3, h3`: its two `.section-label` headings are `<h3>` where every other page uses `<h2>` for the same role.

There is no `prefers-reduced-motion` guard anywhere except one `scroll-behavior` rule: `/experiments/porcine/` runs three infinite CSS animations plus a 1 Hz blinker and `/experiments/etherhoo/` mutates two tables on 0.8 s and 3.5 s timers forever, with no pause control.
The theme toggle button has no accessible name when JavaScript is disabled: its visible label is set by CSS `::before` content, which does not enter accessible-name computation.
The `<h1>` on `/experiments/porcine/` uses glitch pseudo-elements whose CSS `content: attr(data-text)` is folded into the accessible name, so a screen reader announces the title three times.
`blog/posts/art-tech-highlights.md` contains a stray empty markdown link `[]()` that renders as an anchor with no text, producing a nameless tab stop.
The collection filters on `/experiments/poap-vault/` use `role="tab"` with no corresponding tabpanel and no arrow-key handling, so the tab semantics are unbuilt; they behave as filter buttons.
`essentialism/index.html` places its `<meta charset>` beyond the first 1024 bytes of the document because a long comment sits above `<html>`, outside the window browsers use for encoding sniffing.
The `rel="me"` link to YouTube on the home page and on `/profiles/` points at `youtube.com/thebenmeadows`, which returns 404; the `@thebenmeadows` handle form of the URL is the one that resolves.

CRITICAL: Quartz bitmap context draws pixels vertically upside down. In Core Graphics the default coordinate system of a `CGBitmapContext` places the origin (0,0) at the bottom-left corner with Y pointing upward, while the raw buffer returned by `CGBitmapContextGetData` lays pixel rows top-to-bottom starting at row 0. `core/src/imageio.rs` passes the `CGImage` directly to `CGContextDrawImage` without flipping the context transformation matrix, so it renders the image vertically inverted into the pixel array: any valid HEIC (e.g. an iPhone photo) comes out as a JPEG flipped along the Y axis.

Multi-image HEIC: index 0 is the primary by spec. `CGImageSourceGetCount >= 1` and `CreateImageAtIndex(0)` in `core/src/imageio.rs` is right for burst, live photo and animated HEIF, because the primary is item 0 in the `pitm` sense, and `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(0)` on a container with a `thmb` item returns the primary, not the thumb.

The byte order is a constant, not the platform's: `core/src/imageio.rs` passes `K_CG_IMAGE_ALPHA_NONE_SKIP_LAST | K_CG_BITMAP_BYTE_ORDER_DEFAULT` with `K_CG_BITMAP_BYTE_ORDER_DEFAULT = 0`. The value is a literal while the constant's name says "the platform's default", so the R,G,B,X layout the engine reads is not actually tied to the host's byte order.

`CGContextDrawImage` does not colour-convert when the context uses the image's own space. For a Display P3 source in `core/src/imageio.rs`, `ctx_cs` is the image's `CGColorSpace` and the context is 8 bpc; if Image I/O hands back a `CGImage` with extended-range components, values above 1.0 clamp to the per-component max. A real iPhone HDR HEIC decoded by Image I/O as extended range will clamp and bleed at exactly the highlights the Email preset exists to show.

In `core/src/webp.rs`, `PICTURE_CHUNKS` includes `b"VP8X"`, but `VP8X` is the extended feature header, not an image frame bitstream. `VP8X` should be removed from `PICTURE_CHUNKS` so that `has_picture` strictly requires a true frame (`VP8 ` or `VP8L`); every WebP that carries pixels has one of those two chunks at the top level of its RIFF chain.

Clearing the VP8X flags at `out[20]` in `strip_webp` (`core/src/webp.rs`) is safe and correct. Per the WebP container spec `VP8X` must be the first chunk, so the RIFF header is bytes 0..12, the `VP8X` chunk header is bytes 12..20, and the first payload byte holding the feature flags is exactly `out[20]`. The `out.len() > 20` guard prevents out-of-bounds indexing if `VP8X` has a zero-length payload or is cut short, and `&out[12..16] == b"VP8X"` ensures the flags are only modified when `VP8X` is in the first-chunk position.

A WebP containing a picture chunk with a zero-length payload returns `Some` from `strip_webp` (`core/src/webp.rs`) with `wiped > 0`, so the `lib.rs` branch never sees `wiped == 0` and happily emits a "stripped" WebP with a blank picture, which `Source::open` then decodes to an image of nothing through an `unwrap_or`-style fallback rather than reporting the blank. `has_picture` needs a payload-length floor.

The profile is read through the same torn chain: `icc_profile` in `core/src/webp.rs` swallows the walk's `None` and returns `None`, which is indistinguishable from "this file carries no `ICCP`". A wide-gamut WebP cut short in transit therefore loses its profile and comes back untagged, flat, and reported as a success.

Fast-mode PDF rewrites run at core count: `concurrencyLimit` in `app/Sources/JobQueue.swift` returns `cores` unless some job is `.quality`, and a PDF through Shrink is `.fast`, so a batch of PDFs on a 16 GB / 8-core machine runs eight concurrent document rewrites, each holding every decoded picture in a document at once. The 167 MB-per-fast-job figure the concurrency limit rests on was measured for single images, so a PDF batch can exceed it.

`public.heif` likely re-admits AVIF: Apple's UTI tree conforms `public.avif` to `public.heif`, so declaring `public.heif` on the Convert to AVIF Services entry (`app/project.yml`) probably makes Finder offer Convert to AVIF for `.avif` files despite the exclusion, a menu item that always reports failure.

`concurrencyLimit` keys on `job.mode` (`app/Sources/JobQueue.swift`). If `Job` stores a separate `mode` that defaults to `.fast` for preset-created jobs rather than returning `preset.mode`, an AVIF batch runs at core-count concurrency with quality-mode memory, the exact blowup the limit exists to prevent.

Silent semantic loss: `org.webmproject.webp` includes animated WebP and `public.heif` includes HEIF sequences, so converting either through Convert to AVIF yields a still AVIF, silently dropping every frame after the first.

The `landsOnSource` comparison in `app/Sources/JobQueue.swift` is lexical, not filesystem identity. Unicode-normalisation aliases could therefore be a false negative if Foundation constructs the destination with a different normalisation from the source and the volume resolves both to the same entry, letting a conversion be written over its own source.

The queue does not compare `result.data` with the input before writing and marking the job done (`app/Sources/JobQueue.swift`). If an engine mode can succeed with byte-identical output, for example Strip on a file with nothing removable, the app still performs a write and reports completion.

The new inline JSON-LD is probably blocked by the CSP, and fails silently. `index.html:30` adds `<script type="application/ld+json">`; CSP `script-src` applies to inline script elements including non-executable types, so unless `_headers` carries `'unsafe-inline'` or a hash for this block, Chrome and Firefox refuse it and the Person schema never reaches a crawler, with no visible symptom and no build failure.

`unlisted` was wired into three consumers and probably not the fourth. `build-blog.mjs` filters `listed` for the index and blog feed, and `build-search-index.mjs` filters it out of search, but `scripts/build-feed.mjs` is unchanged and, if it reads `pages.json`, the superseded post enters the site release feed and reaches every subscriber at `/feed.xml`, exactly the exposure `unlisted` exists to prevent.

`indentOutsidePre()` in `scripts/build-blog.mjs` evaluates `inPre` before updating state for the current line. On the line opening `
`, `inPre` is false, so the line gets indented by 12 spaces; on the closing `
` line, `inPre` is true, so it receives no indentation. Multi-line `
` blocks therefore output misaligned outer tags in the HTML source.

Tie-breaking in `scripts/build-speaking.mjs` and `scripts/build-ai.mjs` uses `localeCompare()` without an explicit locale parameter (e.g. `a.slug.localeCompare(b.slug)`), so the generated pages can re-order across CI runners or mirrors operating under differing system locales (`LANG`).

Stale state leak on navigation in `src/pages/Jar.tsx`: `details` state is never cleared when `refFilter` changes or is removed (`if (!payments || !refFilter) return`). Navigating from a specific receipt (`?ref=TAB-123`) back to the main jar view leaves stale transaction details in memory, and any matching transaction signatures in the full jar list will erroneously render `<TxShape>` elements despite no reference filter being active.

Open-amount URL link param overwrite allows spoofing/underpayment. When a merchant chooses "Whatever the payer chooses, for a tip jar" in `Create.tsx`, the amount is ignored, but a crafted payload with `a` (or `u`) set alongside an open tip-jar request keeps `a` through `normalizeRequest`, and `Pay.tsx` checks `if (request.amount)` before `isOpenAmount(request)`. A link with `a: "0.000001"` therefore tricks a payer viewing an open tip jar into paying 0.000001 COOK instead of their intended tip: the UI's input expectation and the signed amount disagree.

Multi-account balance consolidation error misleads the payer. `Pay.tsx` displays `holding.spendable` as what the user can send, and `fetchBalanceOf` (`src/lib/balances.ts`) sets `spendable` from the sum of the token accounts, while `chooseSourceAccount` in `src/lib/pay.ts` throws a `PaymentError` when no single account holds `rawAmount`. With 10 tokens in the ATA and 10 in an auxiliary account and a 15-token invoice, the UI allows clicking "Pay 15" but building then fails with "split across 2 accounts... consolidate them first".

`looksLikeName` / `validateRecipient` (`src/lib/names.ts`, `src/lib/request.ts`) misclassify a base58 address ending in `.cook`: `.cook` is five lowercase characters all in the base58 alphabet, so any 32-44-character key ending in those five characters returns true from `looksLikeName` and is forced down the name path, where `resolveRecipient` throws `not registered` and the recipient can never be paid.

The `fetchJarHistory` prefilter in `src/lib/history.ts` relies on `entry.memo`: the RPC memo summary is treated as authoritative, so a node that does not populate it silently drops every real payment and reports "No Cookie Jar payments have reached this address yet", the one wrong answer the comment above `PAGE` says a jar must never give.

`package.json` defines `"live": "tsx scripts/live-check.ts"`, and the README says `npm run live` runs 18 checks against the live chain, but the file `scripts/live-check.ts` does not exist in the repository (the `scripts/` directory is missing), so `npm run live` fails immediately with module not found.

Stale payment state can survive a route change. `Pay.tsx`'s initialization effect does not clear `request`, `resolved`, `priceUsd`, `enteredAmount`, or `holding` when `payload` changes; it only sets `stage` to "reading". Navigating from `#/pay/<A>` to `#/pay/<B>` while the component stays mounted and clicking during B's asynchronous load leaves `payBlocker` null on the stale state, and `pay()` can submit A's payment from the B URL.

Memo separator injection breaks memo structure. `buildMemo` in `src/lib/request.ts` replaces `|` with `/` in `ref` but does not escape `|` in `note`, so a request with `ref = "INV123"` and `note = "foo|bar"` produces `cookiejar:1|INV123|foo|bar`, and `parseMemo` then splits on the wrong separator and returns a ref and note different from what the link creator set.

In `buildPayment` (`src/lib/pay.ts`), when the mint is wrapped COOK (`So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`) the payment is a direct SPL token transfer without unwrapping or handling native lamports, which leaves the funds trapped in a token account if the recipient expected native COOK.

History is pre-filtered on the RPC memo summary: the candidate filter in `fetchJarHistory` (`src/lib/history.ts`) drops transactions when `s.memo` is present but not the jar memo, and `getSignaturesForAddress`'s `memo` field is the first memo's summary, so a payment whose jar memo is the second memo instruction can be silently excluded (false negative).

Precision loss in `usdToRaw` (`src/lib/quote.ts`) is a defect: for `usd = "0.01"`, `priceUsd = 1000000` and `decimals = 2`, the fixed-point division evaluates to `0n` and `usdToRaw` throws `QuoteError`, blocking legitimate payments whenever a dollar amount evaluates below one integer base unit.

`_headers` does not cover the new pages. It grants `max-age=0, must-revalidate` only to `/`, `/morning/`, `/morning/daybreak/`, `/hours/`, `/psalter/` and `/psalter/*`; the pages shipped in the latest releases (`/compline/`, `/evening/rule/`, `/canons/`, `/communion/`, `/communion/canon/`, `/communion/thanksgiving/`) match no rule, so that HTML ships with no Cache-Control at all and browsers may heuristically cache it, serving stale text on first visit before the service worker installs.

In `evening/rule/index.html`, Chrysostom's 24 petitions are wrapped in `<div class="prayer indented">`. Dead rule in `prayers.css`: `.prayer.indented p.opening { text-indent: 0 }` matches nothing, because the only `.opening` paragraphs are in non-indented `.prayer` blocks.

`scripts/check-ai-links.mjs --ci` exits 1 on any non-2xx response, so a 403 or 429 from a venue that blocks scripts fails the run as if the entry were dead.

`scripts/build-speaking.mjs` defines a marked `RENDERER` with only a `paragraph` method, so marked's passthrough `html` renderer still applies and raw `<script>` in a transcript reaches the generated page.

`scripts/build-feed.mjs` writes the commit subject raw into the Atom `<title>` and `<content>` and the RSS `<title>` and `<description>`, so a `<` or `&` in a commit message produces an invalid `feed.xml` and `rss.xml`.

`scripts/sign-release.sh` passes the release key to `nak` as `--sec "$NOSTR_SECRET_KEY"`, so the nsec appears in argv and is visible to every same-uid process during publish, contrary to the script's own header.
`scripts/version-css.mjs` renames `output.css` to its hashed name and exits 0 even when no page references `/output.css`, leaving every page pointing at a stylesheet that no longer exists in `dist/`.

`scripts/build-manifest.mjs` records the build time in the manifest, so Cloudflare and Netlify produce different `manifest.json` bytes for the same commit and the release signature verifies on only one of them.
`scripts/check-onchain-code.mjs` fetches the generator from the TzKT indexer on every run, and `build:netlify` runs it, so a TzKT outage fails every deploy.
`scripts/sync-readme-mirrors.mjs` falls back to printing the raw `kind/network` slug for any pair missing from `LABELS`, so a newly added network ships to `readme.md` as an unlabelled row.
`_headers` caches `/me.png` for a day but has no rule for `/me.webp`, the avatar every current browser actually fetches through the `<picture>` source, so it is revalidated on every navigation.
